summary: Devendra Nath Ojha is an Indologist who completed a certificate programme at the National Sanskrit University in 2020. He was a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Delhi (2011–2013) and Head of Sanskrit and assistant professor at Amity University in 2017.
Deviprasad Mishra is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the French Institute of Pondicherry in 1999. That same year, he held a post there as a researcher and Deputy Head of Indology.
Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).
Dezhung Kunga Gyaltsen studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Gaton Ngawang Lekpa, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and Ngawang Nyima, and was a research project participant at the University of Washington (1960–1972).

Dhananjay Vashistha works in Indology and philosophy after earning a B.E. (Hons) from BITS Pilani (2011–2015). Formerly a network engineer at Cisco Systems and faculty at Trans IAS Academy, he became a research associate at Bhaktivedanta Research Center in 2023.

Dharm P. S. Bhawuk works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1992–1995) and became affiliate faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 1995.

Dharmananda Kosambi (1876–1947) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Harvard University in 1926. He held posts at the University of Calcutta, Gujarat University, Harvard University, and Saint Petersburg State University.

Dhirendra Mohan Datta (1898–1974) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1919–1923). He held academic posts at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).
Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under David Friedman and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He held teaching posts at Open University, the University of Leeds, the University of Bristol, and the University of Chester.
Di Jiang works in linguistics, computational fields, and Tibetology. He has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and as a professor at Jiangsu Normal University.

Di Luo is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Southern California (attested 2016), supervised by Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge, following MA supervision under James Steele.

Diana L. Eck is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned her PhD at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She spent her career at Harvard (~1976–2024) as a professor and later emerita research professor.

Diana Lange works in Tibetology, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She earned degrees from Leipzig, Tibet University, Humboldt University, and the Sorbonne/EPHE. She held research and teaching posts at TU Berlin, Leipzig, Zurich, Museum am Rothenbaum, Humboldt University, and Hamburg.

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. In 2005, she was attested as an adjunct professor of anthropology at both Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane Denis is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a BA at Naropa University and a PhD at Laval University. In 2017, she held an appointment as an associate professor at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Diane E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at UCLA under William M. Bodiford. She has held posts at Kenyon College, Pepperdine University, and Western Michigan University.
Diane L. Howard is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who was attested as a graduate student at McMaster University in 1982, studying under supervisor Graeme MacQueen.
Dickwela Piyananda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the Catholic University of America under doctoral supervisor Siegfried A. Schulz (attested 1974).
